newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas called higher, in line with ACCESS.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas called higher, in line with ACCESS.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open slightly higher Thursday, mirroring the upward move on ACCESS, industry sources said.
July over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.08 to $2.10 after settling to the downside Wednesday at $2.071 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, July last traded 2.5 cents higher at $2.096.
Despite the higher opening call, cash prices at the Henry Hub, La., were talked about three to four cents lower at $2.10-2.11 per mmBtu.
Some traders speculated that downward pressure on futures may surface shortly after the opening.
"They're going to want to test the $2.05 area. If they don't work through that, I think they'll move it back to about $2.10-2.12," one trader said.
Technically, traders said the next backstop for July if it breaks through $2.05-2.065 will be $2. Further resistance was seen at $2.21, then at $2.25, $2.37 and the contract high at $2.44.
AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 91 bcf, at the low end of the 90-100 bcf expected range, and were still 220 bcf, or 21 percent, above year-ago.

Eastern storage, which gained 59 bcf last week, was 104 bcf, or 20 percent, over last year. Producing region stocks rose 21 bcf and remained almost 60 percent above 1996 levels. Western inventories continued to lag year-ago by 14 percent.
In Wednesday's cash, swing gas in the Louisiana Gulf was unchanged in the mid-teens. Midcon pipes also held steady at $2.01-2.03. New York city gate gas was flat around $2.43.
Separately, Mobil Corp said its Mary Ann gas processing plant, with a capacity of 380-390 million cubic feet per day, will likely be fully restored by this weekend.
Planned maintenance at the plant, in Coden, Ala., began in mid-May. As of Wednesday night, the company said about 68 percent of capacity had been restored.
